dedupe_keys.name: building level urban flood damage assessment for a 50 year rainfall in miyun town beijing

description: This case study applies a lightweight, GIS-based automated method to estimate flood damage building by building in Miyun Town, in the transition zone between the piedmont plain and the mountains of Beijing, where complex terrain and limited drainage make severe urban flooding likely. It is published as a chapter in Hydraulic and Civil Engineering Technology X (Advances in Transdisciplinary Engineering, IOS Press, 21 November 2025) by Chun-Pin Tseng and colleagues at the Qilu Institute of Technology, with a co-author from Brandeis University. The framework combines a high-resolution elevation model, building vector data and custom depth-damage curves in ArcGIS with Python scripting. For a 50-year return-period rainfall, 4,961 buildings are affected with an estimated loss of RMB 2.462 billion, 68.48 per cent in residential and 31.52 per cent in commercial buildings; underground commercial facilities show the highest loss per unit area, and validation errors stay within plus or minus 5 per cent. Coverage: Miyun Town, Beijing. Access: open-access chapter. Licence: CC BY-NC 4.0; free. Caveats: one rainfall scenario and no drainage network data. Simulation uses: a template for building-level flood loss estimation where data are scarce. Related records: the USGS HERA exposure data and the wood-frame flood fragility data.
name: Building-level urban flood damage assessment for a 50-year rainfall in Miyun Town, Beijing
outcomes: For a 50-year rainfall, 4,961 buildings are affected with a loss of about RMB 2.462 billion, 68.48 per cent residential and 31.52 per cent commercial; validation gave errors within plus or minus 5 per cent.
